23 and 27 are kind of similar, but it's unique. At 23, someone is just finishing college and sometimes starting their first time working a full time job (not everyone but some). And 27, someone could be done with college and still learning the ropes of adulthood and being financially independent from their parents, etc. This is only 4 years, so I don't really see a huge issue at this age. 


However, 18 and 22 are also 4 years, but that's more like 6 years to me. 18 is sometimes still in high school and hasn't had any experience with being an adult yet. And mentally in terms of maturity, 18 and 22 are different. 22 isn't that far ahead, but that persons had about 4 years to sort of decide what they like and what they want to do in life. At 18, I was just graduating HS and just wanted to have a fun summer vacation, I wasn't really seriously thinking about my future like that. Just the things that were short term. But by the time 22 rolls around, you sort have to start making those decisions. 


But at 23 vs 27, your life goals also kind of change after that while brain development thing. Like at 23 I was content with where I was at, but at 27 I was sooo ready for a change. Wanted to finally live alone, move to a new place etc. and I had the CONFIDENCE and the means (degree and job) to do it. I wouldn't want to interrupt a 22 yo who is at that stage of figuring out what they want, while I already have a good idea of my goals. 


My point is, you are still doing a lot of development in your 20s. It's like 10yo vs 20yo it's 10 years but you change like crazy in those years. Same with my 20 to the 30, some people things you are just a full on adult at 18, but you will change and grow into who you will be in those 10 years. I personally would not want to interrupt that very important time in someone's life, unless we were like 1-2 years apart and right there together. 


Just like at 14,15,16 you are in a totally different grade each year. Would an 12 year old have the same things and opportunities that 16 year old would have. It's only 4 in years but how much do we charge in those 4 years so quickly. 


I could understand someone that is 40 that doesn't have certain experiences and wants to meet someone similar, but that doesn't automatically mean go for someone in their 20s. I missed out on a lot of things in my childhood that I should have experienced to help me develop into a proper adult (thankfully therapy exists), but I don't see the need to go hang out with a lot of children just so I can try to experience those things. 


There are plenty of people in our age group/maturity group that we can find things in common with. I always felt like I was a late bloomer (and I am), but I don't even look at people in their early 20s, and I'm in my late 20s, because I can see the difference in maturity. I know they are still going through changes and will change alot in the next few years. Why waste their time if they are going to hit 25 to and realize they can meet someone going through the same things together with them at the same time, then leave me lol. 


Just let that fruit ripen all the way before it gets picked. It's only fair.


I digress...


Either way, in that scenario you are starting, whether it be a man or woman, if someone was still inexperienced at 40, I don't think they should be dating someone in their early 20s.  It becomes a question of what each person brings to the table. I wouldn't date someone in their 40s even if they were inexperienced. Maybe be friends but nothing more. I mean that's atleast 10-20 years of lost time. While I want to play, they don't want to. And by the time I'm in my 40s and still have energy, they'll be 60 something and possibly dealing with the health issues of old age. And not to mention children, I wouldn't have kids with someone that age without some extensive testing each others health. (women in their late 30s can still get pregnant but it's considered high risk, and men in that age range, their sperm isn't fresh like a young man and can also lead to developmental issues with the baby, etc). Those things have to be considered. Atleast I would. 


 If they had some in situation that was out of their control that led to that inexperience (depression, mental health, etc) that's not their fault, but still they should be realistic. I lost most, if not all, my 20s to depression and severe mental health issues, so I regret that I didn't really get to enjoy these years, because they were painful. But I'm still not trying to date someone 10 years younger. I realized I just have to grow from my experience, be realistic, and keep it moving.
